newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH BANKA HANA SETS RIGHTS ISSUE - AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH BANKA HANA SETS RIGHTS ISSUE - AGENCY.

text.p: Czech bank, Banka Hana a.s., said on Friday it planned to raise its basic capital to 1.99 billion crowns from the current 499 million crowns through a rights issue later this year, the local agency CTK reported.

It quoted bank officials in Prostejov, Moravia, where the bank is based, as saying the first round of the issue would run from October 24 to November 7, and offer 499,174 new shares with a nominal value of 1,000 crowns each for 1,200 crowns.
Unsubscribed shares would then be offered to the public at 1,300 crowns in a second round, it said.

The equity increase, which is still subject to approval by a general meeting of shareholders on September 30, would raise the bank's capital adequacy ratio to over nine percent, Oldrich Skulil, a bank official told CTK.
Bank officials were not immediately available for further comment.
CTK said Belgian-based Kredietbank Brussels had raised its stake in Banka Hana to over 10 percent, but the exact shareholding was not available.
